title: Adaptive precision canary with automated rollback for calibration regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We want to safely deploy FP8/INT8 quantized variants of production models. Current canary rollouts surface occasional calibration regressions (accuracy drop on targeted prompt sets) that are hard to detect early and cause customer-visible quality degradation. Goal: implement an adaptive-precision canary and automated rollback mechanism that combines live-sampled calibration, statistical accuracy gates, and a fast fallback path to a compatible higher-precision variant when quality checks fail. This ticket covers design, implementation, and observability for the runtime-side rollback and canary gating logic.
acceptance_criteria: Canaries may run in two adaptive modes: precision-sweep (INT8->FP8->FP16) and cost-first (FP8 primary, INT8 fallback) selectable per-route.
Calibration harness collects live-sampled inputs (0.1%-1% sampling) and replays them offline against quant profiles within 1 hour of canary launch.
Automated rollback triggers when a canary exceeds predefined regression thresholds on at least two statistical tests (token-level KL, emission overlap, and task-specific metric) with p<0.05.
Fallback is executed within 30s of trigger detection and preserves in-flight requests (graceful switchover) with <10% spike in tail latency.
Dashboard shows canary health, per-route accuracy delta, sample count, and rollback reasons. Alerts to SRE/PM on high-severity regressions.
End-to-end test covering a synthetic regression scenario that induces rollback and verifies metrics/alerting are emitted.
Runbook created for manual override and post-mortem steps.
Feature flags gated for initial rollout: enable_adaptive_canary, enable_auto_fallback.
No customer traffic should be routed to a quantized variant after a confirmed rollback for that route until re-verification completes.
Latency SLA maintained: median increase <=5ms, 99th <= +30ms during switchover for affected requests.
implementation_notes: Canary controller will be extended with adaptive-precision state machine: PROBE -> OBSERVE -> EVALUATE -> PROMOTE / ROLLBACK.
Calibration worker will ingest live-sampled requests and run batch calibration jobs per profile (FP8/INT8) using existing calib harness; store calibration artifacts with monotonic versioning.
Introduce accuracy validator service with three tests: KL divergence on token distributions, top-k emission overlap, and task-specific comparator (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE for tasks with references).
Statistical gating uses sequential hypothesis testing (alpha=0.05) and requires minimum N samples (configurable, default 250) before evaluation window closes.
Rollback path: immediate routing change to 'compatible-fallback' flavor (FP16-compatible model variant or unquantized build) plus quick metric backfill to confirm stability.
Graceful switchover uses per-connection KV-locking to ensure in-flight KV-cache continuity for decoder models; runtime will copy a minimal set of cache entries when switching flavors.
Circuit-breaker metrics: consecutive_failures, recent_pvalue, sample_age, effect_size; used to avoid noisy-rollback loops.
Expose feature flags and per-customer config: canary_sample_rate, required_sample_count, rollback_sensitivity.
Unit tests for validator thresholds and e2e integration in staging. Performance test simulating 10k req/s with 0.5% sampling.
Migration plan: start with internal-only routes (non-critical), then expand to low-traffic customer segments before full rollout.
monitoring_plan: New dashboard: quant-canary/{route}/health showing sample_count, KL_delta, topk_overlap, p_value, rollback_count, current_precision.
Alert: QUANT_CANARY_REGRESSION (SEV2) when p_value<0.05 AND effect_size>threshold AND sample_count>=min_samples.
Alert: QUANT_CANARY_NO_SAMPLES (SEV3) if sample_count < min_samples after 60m of canary runtime.
Log format: quant_canary_event (route, canary_id, profile, samples, metrics, action_taken, trace_id).
Retention: store sampled inputs and metric deltas for 90 days for audit and replay; mask PII via existing redaction pipeline before storage.
SLO checks: rolling-7d false-positive rollback rate <1% for mature routes.
rollback_policy_summary: If the accuracy validator detects a statistically significant regression (default alpha=0.05) AND the effect size exceeds route-configured tolerance, the controller performs an automated rollback to the configured compatible-fallback (usually FP16/unquantized flavor). The rollback includes a fast routing change, metric emission, and a hold period (default 24h) during which the quantized variant is blocked for that route unless manual re-approve occurs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Noisy signals from low-sample routes -> Mitigation: require minimum sample_count and use sequential testing to reduce false positives.
Risk: Latency spike on switchover due to cache transfer -> Mitigation: incremental cache copy and warmup traffic to fallback pool before cutover.
Risk: Masking of regressions by A/B traffic mixing -> Mitigation: deterministic routing for canaries and per-customer isolation during evaluation window.
Risk: Storage costs for sampled payloads -> Mitigation: sample-rate tuning, aggressive redaction, 90-day retention cap.
Risk: Security/compliance for sampled requests -> Mitigation: redaction and KMS encryption of stored artifacts; access control via Private console roles.
notes: Spike outcomes (2026-02-15): FP8 provided 18-28% compute reduction vs FP16 on our transformer benchmarks, INT8 gave 30-45% in throughput but had larger variance on long-tail prompts.
Design review 2026-02-28: PM and SRE requested explicit p-value and sample_count criteria and a 24h hold window post-rollback.
Staging run 2026-03-05: induced synthetic regression via weight perturbation; automated rollback executed in 22s, 99p latency increased by 8ms during switchover and returned to baseline thereafter.
